title: Write output volume through pactl, not the node-bound setter

leads.summary: Coalescing uses only the percentage, not the sink identity, so a same-percent request for a newly selected sink is discarded
leads.consequence: While a pactl write of 50% to sink A is running, switch output to B and move B's slider to 50%. pendingOutputVolume and sentOutputVolume both equal 50; the writer's onExited clears the request, leaving B unchanged. If the sink vanishes with a different percentage queued, sendOutputVolume returns without draining that request and the next relative step can use an obsolete target. Track sink name with each pending and active write, and re-evaluate or clear state when the target changes or disappears.
leads.triage: behavioural; neutral follow-up to Opus (opus/followup-1.md) confirmed from source; published as source-only finding N2 with corrected fix wording

leads.summary: A pactl launch failure leaves the pending percentage stuck; nonzero exits silently discard the target
leads.consequence: If pactl cannot start, Quickshell 0.3.1 emits runningChanged but no exited, so the callback that clears pendingOutputVolume never runs. A later relative step starts from the unsent percentage rather than the live volume. If pactl starts but exits nonzero (sink removed or server unavailable), onExited ignores exitCode and clears the target as if it succeeded. Add explicit failed-start and exit-status handling, clear or reconcile the failed target, and surface an error when appropriate.
leads.triage: start-failure part already in Opus final (minor observations); nonzero exit covered by Opus follow-up 1: dropped write is appropriate, previous head behaved the same; not published

leads.summary: Scrolling the slider itself can lose relative steps while the writer catches up
leads.consequence: PanelSlider's own wheel handler computes the next step from liveValue, not pendingOutputVolume, and its onValueChanged resets liveValue to an in-flight server echo when not dragging. For example, with an initial 50%, wheel to 55%, wheel to 60% before the first write finishes, then receive the 55% server echo while 60% is pending; a third wheel step asks for 60%, not 65%. The output bar wheel and keyboard now use the pending base, but this slider-wheel caller still does not. Route slider-wheel relative events through the pending base or keep wheel liveValue insulated from intermediate echoes.
leads.triage: already in Opus final as N1 (measured); corroboration noted

leads.summary: Open PR #13004 independently writes this same audio panel for the same issue; keeping both changes makes the tests inconsistent
leads.consequence: PR #13004 is also open, has the identical base SHA, and adds a second serial pactl writer to the same setOutputVolume and Process region. Its setOutputVolume preserves volumeSink.audio.volume = volume, which this PR's test explicitly rejects. A combined version retaining both implementations has duplicate writers and fails this PR's assertion; coordinate or choose a single implementation when resolving the overlap.
leads.triage: factual; verified by coordinator via read-only gh api (hunter-check/pr13004*) and by Opus (related-prs-check.txt); published as a brief related-PR note

leads.summary: Open PR #8871 raises the output slider to 125%, but this PR's new helper caps the pactl argv at 100%
leads.consequence: If both features land with #8871's 125% slider limit and this PR's outputVolumeCommand unchanged, requests between 101 and 125% display an allowed value but write 100% through pactl. Reconcile the helper maximum and tests if the 125% feature merges.
leads.triage: factual; verified by coordinator (hunter-check/pr8871*) and Opus; published in the related-PR note

leads.summary: The new coalescing tests check source patterns, not the described writer behavior
leads.consequence: The new assertions verify a Process declaration and regex text for pending/sent comparison, but never emit moved events, switch sinks, inject a Process exit, or assert the final command sequence; the H1-H3 edge cases can pass them unchanged. Extract the queue policy into a testable pure helper with sink identity or add a sandboxed QML behavior fixture.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (mutants M1-M4, M7 pass 30/30); published as Optional test improvement

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13099#issuecomment-5825734102) and the [author reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13099#issuecomment-5833496023), checked at `a185d2c3`.

**Verified:** the single coalescing writer fixes the write ordering, and the bar wheel and keyboard h/l no longer lost steps in the test harness described below. The balance behaviour is now documented, and the argv helper is unit-tested. One relative-step path was missed: scrolling over the panel's own output slider still loses steps at fast wheel rates.

| Earlier finding | Status at `a185d2c3` |
|---|---|
| Rapid input spawns unordered, uncoalesced writes | Resolved for write ordering, the bar wheel and h/l (harness below). The slider wheel still loses steps (below) |
| Single percentage resets left/right balance | Resolved: kept deliberately and documented in `Panel.qml` and `Model.js`, matching `omarchy-audio-output-volume` |
| Optional test improvement (argv in `Model.js`) | Resolved as suggested. The Panel-level assertions still only match text (note below) |
| Description says "all Bluetooth outputs" | Still present in the PR description |
| Input volume path (`setInputVolume`, Microphone widget) | Unchanged. Not retested; outside this PR's stated scope |

**Verified** from Quickshell 0.3.1 `process.cpp`: `running` turns true as soon as the process is started, so the `!outputVolumeWriter.running` guard cannot start two writers in one tick. `onFinished` clears the process before emitting `exited`, so setting `running = true` inside `onExited` starts the next write. From `pactl` 17.0 source, a successful `pactl` exits only after the server acknowledges the set, so writes cannot reorder. In a headless Quickshell 0.3.1 harness with the PR's writer and step handlers pasted verbatim, on private PipeWire 1.6.8 null sinks, a same-tick burst of 6 steps started `pactl` twice and ended on the expected value. Runs that lost at least one step (bar wheel, 6 × +5% from 30%):

| Bar wheel, 6 steps | same tick or next turn | 1-3 ms apart | 4 ms | 5 ms or more |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Previous head (`130e4ad6`) | 20/20 | 30/30 | 6/10 | 2/50 |
| This head | 0/40 | 0/60 | 0/20 | 0/80 |

Keyboard h/l at this head lost no step in 110 runs.

### Scrolling over the output slider still loses steps

`PanelSlider.onWheel` steps from `liveValue` (`shell/Ui/PanelSlider.qml` 140-147), and `onValueChanged` copies every server readback into `liveValue` (28). The panel binds the slider to `value: root.outputVolume` (`Panel.qml` 871). A readback of an earlier write that arrives while a newer value is queued resets `liveValue`, so the next step recomputes a value that is already queued:

```text
wheel +5%  -> liveValue 35%  -> pactl 35%       (in flight)
wheel +5%  -> liveValue 40%  -> pending 40%     (writer busy)
readback 35% arrives         -> liveValue 35%
wheel +5%  -> liveValue 40%  -> pending 40%     (step lost)
```

Same harness (sink starts at 30%; the expected end value is 60%):

| Slider wheel, 6 steps | same tick or next turn | 1-3 ms apart | 4 ms | 5 ms or more |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| This head | 0/40 lossy | 59/60 lossy, 1 to 4 steps lost | 1/20 | 0/80 |
| Base setter, same slider code | 0/20 | 0/30 | 0/10 | 0/30 |
| Suggested change below | 0/20 | 0/30 | 0/10 | 0/30 |

The base and suggested-change rows cover spacings up to 8 ms.

**Impact:** the slider loses steps only when wheel events come faster than one `pactl` round trip (median 3 ms, at most 10 ms in this lab). `PanelSlider` treats every wheel event as a full 5% step, so high-resolution wheels and touchpads may do that, especially on a busy machine. On the null sinks tested (plain node volume, no card Route), base lost no steps, so this is a regression there. Base was not tested on hardware sinks with a card Route. On Bluetooth routes without `volumeStep`, base wrote nothing at all, so the PR is still a net improvement there.

**Suggested change:** use one target property for all three relative paths, and bind the slider to it:

```qml
readonly property real outputTarget: pendingOutputVolume >= 0 ? pendingOutputVolume / 100 : outputVolume
// output PanelSlider:           value: root.outputTarget
// bar wheel and adjustVolume:   base = root.outputTarget
```

With the slider bound this way, 0 of 90 harness runs lost a step.

**Optional test improvement:** the new Panel assertions match source text only. A copy of head with `outputVolumeWriter.running = true` removed performs no write at all and still passes all 30 assertions. So do copies that drop the replay in `onExited`, or make the bar wheel or h/l ignore the pending value. Moving the resend-or-clear decision and the relative-step base into pure `Model.js` helpers would let the unit tests cover them.

### A device switch during an in-flight write can drop or misbase a request (source reading only)

The pending and sent state holds only a percentage (`Panel.qml` 439-447, 618-624). If the output device changes during an in-flight write, `onExited` drops a request for the new device made before that write finishes, when it has the same percentage as the in-flight write to the old one. Relative steps made in that window build on the old device's level.

**Impact:** this needs an automatic output switch (for example a Bluetooth connect or disconnect) during a fast scroll burst, within one `pactl` write, so it is uncommon.

**Suggested change:** store the target sink name with each pending value, send to that name, and resend when either the percentage or the sink differs. Relative steps would then build on the pending value only while its sink is still the current one.

**Related open PRs:** #13004 fixes the same issue (#12886) in the same `setOutputVolume` and `Process` region with a separate `pactl` queue. #8871 raises the output maximum to 125%, while `Model.outputVolumeCommand` here clamps at 100%. If #8871 lands later, the helper and its `100%` assertion would need the new maximum.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** source review of `a185d2c3` against Quickshell 0.3.1, PipeWire 1.6.8 and `pactl` 17.0. The repository test ran at head, the previous head and base, with disposable mutants. Write ordering and step loss were measured in a headless Quickshell 0.3.1 harness with the PR's writer, step handlers and slider logic pasted verbatim. The harness used private PipeWire and pipewire-pulse servers on null sinks, with simulated wheel and keyboard input. It was not the full panel, and no Bluetooth card Route or hardware was used. The device-switch note is from source reading only.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
